subject: Unscheduled: scheduler consistency micro-patch — short window & verification
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@blueskyanalytics.com>, ops@blueskyanalytics.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Sep 2029 02:12:00 +0000
Subject: Unscheduled: scheduler consistency micro-patch — short window & verification

Hi Alex / BlueSky ops team,

Quick heads-up — we observed a small uptick (0.4% of requests) in transient request failures (503 / short timeouts) across the east-us serving pool starting ~2029-09-21 01:40 UTC. Our on-call traced this to an intermittent race in the prefetch/scheduler path that can cause temporary KV-cache alignment drift for a subset of long-running sessions.

We prepared a non-invasive micro-patch that addresses the race by adding a coordination barrier and an additional sanity-check on KV offsets. We'll be rolling this patch to east-us instances in a controlled, staggered window starting at 2029-09-21 05:00 UTC and expect the full rollout to complete within ~90 minutes. Expected customer impact: transient 30–90s request latency spikes for <0.5% of traffic during a node restart; no user data loss.

What we need from you:
- Confirm you can avoid scheduling large inference batches (long streaming sessions or multi-turn inference sweeps) between 05:00–06:30 UTC.
- If you have any pinned model versions or dedicated pools in east-us, please let us know immediately so we can coordinate a zero-downtime path or postpone to a separate maintenance window.

Attachments: scheduler_patch_notes_v1.2.pdf (release notes & rollback plan), smoke_test_plan.txt (customer-facing checks).

If you prefer we can delay until your local off-peak window; otherwise we’ll proceed at 05:00 UTC to minimize risk of further client-facing errors.

Thanks — Sean
--
Sean Gallagher
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Moreno <alex@blueskyanalytics.com>

Cc: ops@blueskyanalytics.com
Date: Sat, 21 Sep 2029 02:47:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unscheduled: scheduler consistency micro-patch — short window & verification

Thanks Sean — appreciate the quick note. A couple quick questions:
1) Can you confirm the exact rollback procedure if the patch causes increased error rates? We need an explicit rollback timeline for our incident playbook.
2) Do you have a brief list of smoke checks we can run from our side post-deploy? If you can paste 3–4 commands/requests we can run immediately that would be helpful.

We can avoid large batches in that window but have two pinned endpoints in east-us that serve low-latency traffic; please loop in any svc owners if you plan node restarts that target pinned pools.

— Alex
Alex Moreno
Head of Platform, BlueSky Analytics
alex@blueskyanalytics.com | +1 617-222-8888

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@blueskyanalytics.com>, ops@blueskyanalytics.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Sep 2029 14:35:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unscheduled: scheduler consistency micro-patch — short window & verification

Alex — thanks for the quick reply and the callout on pinned endpoints. Short update and the post-deploy verification summary below.

1) Timeline & rollback- We proceeded with the controlled rollout at 05:00 UTC after confirming BlueSky's pinned pools would be excluded. The patch was staged (canary on 5% of nodes) at 05:00–05:20, then ramped to 25% at 05:20–05:40, and completed to 100% by 06:25 UTC.
- Rollback plan: If we had seen an increase above our threshold (error-rate delta > 0.8% sustained for 10m), we would have initiated an automated rollback to the previous binary and rebalanced traffic; that path is documented in scheduler_patch_notes_v1.2.pdf (attached) and in JIRA-7832. No rollback was required — metrics improved immediately (median latency down 12%, error rate back to baseline).

2) Customer smoke checks (quick copy/paste):
- POST /v1/generate with 3 concurrent short requests (synchronous) using your low-latency model endpoint: expect 200 responses within 1.2x normal P50
- Run the sample streaming session for ~60s and verify no dropouts (we provide a script in smoke_test_plan.txt)
- Check your request logs for any increase in 5xx counts in the 05:00–07:00 UTC window (should be at or below baseline)

3) Artifacts & attachments
- scheduler_patch_notes_v1.2.pdf — release notes, canary progression, rollback steps (customer-facing & technical)
- smoke_test_plan.txt — three scripted checks to validate behavior (included)
- postdeploy-verify-logs-20290921.zip — anonymized aggregation of our smoke runs and metrics (attached)

4) Follow-ups & next steps
- We will open a short postmortem with timeline and root-cause write-up early next week; preliminary cause: an edge-case race inside the prefetch scheduler when a KV eviction coincides with a session rehydrate. We have a follow-up fix scheduled that removes the fragile code path and adds fuzz testing to prevent regressions.
- Marissa is looping in Billing to evaluate a small service credit given the customer-facing disruption; she will reach out separately if there's an authorization.
- Priya will send an optional patch that further reduces node-restart latency for pinned pools (if you want us to run that, tell us your preferred maintenance window).

Thanks again for coordinating quickly. If you want a short 15m bridge to walk through the artifacts I can set that up this afternoon.

Best — Sean
--
Sean Gallagher
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198
Redwood Inference
